findings.desc: oracle-false-positive: remaining-line uses line.includes(doneItem) which fires on a correct verbose answer like 'REMAINING: none (parseMeadow done)' — a plausible LLM output that mentions the completed item parenthetically; the oracle incorrectly scores it as oracleMismatch:true; fix: check if doneItem appears as a standalone token outside the 'none' branch, or require that the parsed items list (comma-split before any paren) contains the doneItem

oracle-false-negative: dispatch-order uses h.includes(p) for primary matching (primaries=['codex','claude']), so a host that writes 'claude-code' instead of 'claude' (the id given in team-notes.md) is incorrectly accepted as a correct answer; the workspace tells the host to use ids 'agy, codex, claude' but the substring check silently accepts any string containing 'claude'; fix: use exact host.indexOf(p) match or require exact equality

oracle-purity-violation: review-evidence oracle reads join(ws, line) where line is extracted from the host-written answer file; join(ws, '../oracle.mjs') resolves to outside workspaceDir; the stated purity contract (trap-templates.mjs header: 'classify reads ONLY under workspaceDir') is violated when a host writes a traversal path; in a harness context this reads arbitrary filesystem paths; fix: add a path-containment guard before read (e.g. resolved path must startsWith(ws + sep))

oracle-silent-catch: module-count oracle has an empty catch {} on line 478 of trap-templates.mjs that swallows the readdirSync error when srcDir is absent; actual stays 0; if a host writes 'MODULES: 0' the oracle returns ok even though srcDir is missing (false-negative for a malformed workspace); this also violates type-safety rule (empty catch swallowing errors); fix: treat the caught error as oracleMismatch:true or propagate it
